To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the long-term follow-up of MAINTAIN did not show a benefit for MMF over AZA as maintenance treatment of proliferative lupnepritis; (ii) early decrease of 0.5 gram proteinuria is an excellent prognostic marker for long-term renal prognosis; (iii) the positive predictive value of the 0.5 g proteinuria cut-off is independent of the addition of renal function and urine analysis to the definition of early response.

10-year renal outcome was similar between AZA and MFM, and that a 24 hour proteinuria decrease to less than 0.5 g/day within the first 3 months of therapy was a strong predictor of long-term renal response.

the 10-year data of the MAiNTAIN Nephritis trial do not support the superiority of mycophenolic acid over azathioprine as maintenance treatment for lupus nephritis and that the excellent positive predictive power of an early decrease of proteinuria for long-term renal remission is not affected by including renal function and urination in the definition of early response.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MAINTAIN trial did not show that mycophenolic acid is superior to azathioprine as maintenance therapy in Caucasian patients with proliferative lupus glomerulonephritis, and that the early decrease of proteinuria has an excellent positive predictive value for the long-term outcome.
the long-term follow-up of this trial, comparing azathioprines and mycophenalate mofetil in the maintenance therapy of lupuus nephritis, did not indicate that mycophenalates were superior.
the long-term follow-up of this trial did not show that MMF is better than AZA as maintenance treatment of proliferative lupnepritis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long-term follow-up of MAINTAIN Nethritis Trial does not indicate that MM is superior to AZ as maintenance therapy in Caucasian population suffering from Proliferative LN.
MMF is not superior to AZA for long term maintenance therapy for proliferative lupus.
MMF and AZA are equally good maintenance therapies for lupus nephritis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early proteinuria response remains a very good prognostic marker of long-term renal survival.
the MAINTAIN trial does not support a superiority of MMF over AZA in Caucasian patients with proliferative LN.
we confirm the value of a 50% proteinuria reduction as a predictor for good renal outcome.
